en.headline: Middle-aged engineer loses HK$8.5 million in online romance scam
en.dek: Police said at least 18 romance scam reports were received in the past week with total losses exceeding HK$13 million, including this case involving a fake Taiwanese dancer.
body: Police said a middle-aged engineer lost more than HK$8.5 million after being drawn into an online romance scam involving a woman who claimed to be a dancer at a private club in Taiwan.

According to a post on the force’s CyberDefender anti-scam page, the man met the woman through a dating app and the pair communicated frequently on WhatsApp. A person posing as her manager then repeatedly asked him to transfer money for “popularity votes” for a dance exam, club fees, asset checks and arrangements to meet, saying he would otherwise not be allowed to see her.

Within half a month the victim transferred the sum to 17 bank accounts designated by the scammers. When an additional “administrative fee” was demanded, he had no money left and the scammers stopped responding.

Police said they had received at least 18 reports of online romance scams in the past week, with total losses exceeding HK$13 million. They urged the public not to transfer money to people they had never met in person and to seek advice from relatives or friends if in doubt.

zh.headline: 中年工程師墮網上情緣騙局 損失逾850萬元
zh.dek: 警方表示過去一周接獲至少18宗網上情緣騙案，總損失逾1,300萬元，其中一宗涉假冒台灣舞者。
body: 警方表示，一名中年工程師在網上情緣騙局中損失超過850萬港元。騙徒假冒台灣私人會所舞者，誘使他不斷轉帳。
根據警方「守網者」反騙專頁周一的帖文，受害人透過交友應用程式結識自稱舞者的女子，雙方在WhatsApp頻繁聯絡。其後有人冒充她的「經理」，以購買舞蹈考試「人氣票」、會所會費、資產查核及安排見面等借口，多次要求他轉帳，並稱否則不獲准見面。
受害人在半個月內將款項分轉至騙徒指定的17個銀行帳戶，總額逾850萬元。當對方再要求支付「行政費」時，他已無餘款，騙徒隨即失聯。
警方指，過去一周接獲至少18宗網上情緣騙案，總損失超過1,300萬元。警方呼籲市民切勿向從未見面的網友轉帳，如有懷疑應先與親友商量。
